recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing handoff with a state transformer (in-memory state schema changed).
justification: the layout of in-memory state changed, so no in-process mechanism can keep the old objects; the new process needs the old state mapped to the new schema (Kitsune/MCR-style state transfer)
a transformer skeleton was generated (old -> new, field by field, TODOs for added/retyped fields)

S6 blockers (2): github.com/gotify/server/v3/api/stream.client.startWriteHandler: long-running function may never quiesce; running activations keep old code; github.com/gotify/server/v3/api/stream.client: layout of in-memory state type changed
alternatives: rolling update if losing the in-memory state is acceptable (cold caches)
risks: changed functions are small enough to be inlined; with S6 slot trampolines the call still dispatches through the slot, but raw binary patching (internal/livepatch) must also patch the inlining callers: github.com/gotify/server/v3/api/stream.API.Handle
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 5 functions
type information is partial (363/363 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
state transformer must be completed and reviewed; encoding/json does not carry unexported fields, so the S5 state envelope needs an explicit DTO for them
